options: Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
Bearings are measured clockwise from north.
A bearing is measured anticlockwise from east.
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. North arrows and quadrants define the convention at every point. Using the wrong reference rotates or reflects the route and changes its angles.

questions.prompt: Angles of elevation and depression — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: The calculated height above the observer’s eye always equals the full tower height.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
Total height includes the eye height when ground levels match.
questions.explanation: Total height includes the eye height when ground levels match. The triangle’s vertical side begins at the observer’s horizontal eye line. Add the stated eye height after finding that vertical difference.

questions.prompt: Quartiles, outliers and modified box plots — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: The upper whisker ends at the largest observed value inside the upper fence.
The upper whisker always ends at Q3+1.5IQR.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
questions.explanation: The upper whisker ends at the largest observed value inside the upper fence. The fence is a cutoff and may not be an observation. Use actual non-outlier values for whisker endpoints.

questions.prompt: Trigonometry in linked three-dimensional triangles — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
The horizontal distance is the ground diagonal between the two corners.
Use the courtyard width alone for elevation from a diagonally opposite corner.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
questions.explanation: The horizontal distance is the ground diagonal between the two corners. Find it from both perpendicular ground dimensions. The elevation triangle must lie in the vertical plane through that diagonal.

options: Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
An interval probability subtracts the lower cumulative area from the upper.

questions.prompt: Heron’s rule and three-side area — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: Heron’s s is the full perimeter.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
Heron’s s is half the perimeter.
questions.explanation: Heron’s s is half the perimeter. The factors s−a, s−b and s−c use the semiperimeter. Using the full perimeter changes every factor and gives an incorrect area.

questions.prompt: Right-triangle ratios and inverse angles — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: Opposite and adjacent depend on the reference angle.
Opposite and adjacent are fixed labels regardless of the chosen acute angle.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
questions.explanation: Opposite and adjacent depend on the reference angle. Only hypotenuse has the same label for either acute angle. Relabel the known and unknown sides before choosing a ratio.

questions.prompt: Sine rule with opposite side–angle pairs — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
A side pairs with the angle opposite it.
A side pairs with the angle touching it in the sine rule.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
questions.explanation: A side pairs with the angle opposite it. Use the same opposite-pair convention in both fractions. An adjacent pairing can give a plausible numerical result that belongs to no valid triangle.

questions.prompt: Planning a statistical investigation — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
Sample size reduces some random variability but does not automatically remove selection bias.
Increasing a convenience sample always removes selection bias.
questions.explanation: Sample size reduces some random variability but does not automatically remove selection bias. An unrepresentative selection method can remain biased even with many observations. Improve the design and describe its limits before generalising.

questions.prompt: Normal percentiles and central intervals — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: The central 80% interval uses the 20th and 80th percentiles.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
A central 80% interval uses the 10th and 90th percentiles.
questions.explanation: A central 80% interval uses the 10th and 90th percentiles. Twenty percent lies outside and is split equally into the two tails. Subtract the percentile probabilities to check the enclosed probability.

questions.prompt: Slope, intercepts and straight-line graphs — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?

Numerical slope depends on coordinate changes and axis units.
A visually steeper line must have the larger slope even when graph scales differ.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
questions.explanation: Numerical slope depends on coordinate changes and axis units. Different scales can alter the visual angle without changing the underlying rate. Compare Δy/Δx in common units.

questions.prompt: Simultaneous linear equations and plan comparisons — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
The intersection identifies equal cost at one usage level.
Finding an intersection proves the same plan is cheaper at every usage level.
questions.explanation: The intersection identifies equal cost at one usage level. Plans with different slopes can swap which is cheaper across it. Compare costs within the practical domain on both sides.

questions.prompt: Comparing group distributions — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: A smaller group median proves every member has a smaller value.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
A median comparison describes centres rather than every individual.
questions.explanation: A median comparison describes centres rather than every individual. Group distributions can overlap even when their medians differ. Use individual data or stronger bounds to establish an all-member statement.

questions.prompt: Building linear models from words — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: Round down when a fractional maximum limits the number of complete affordable units.
An affordability maximum for complete items should always be rounded up.
Changing measurement units changes every dimensionless ratio.
A worked example proves the rule for every possible situation.
questions.explanation: Round down when a fractional maximum limits the number of complete affordable units. Rounding up can exceed the budget. Substitute the chosen integer to check the practical constraint.

The angle must be included between the two chosen sides.
Any angle in the triangle can be used with any two sides in 0.5ab sinC.

questions.explanation: The angle must be included between the two chosen sides. The height interpretation relies on that side-angle pairing. Using a different angle produces the wrong perpendicular component.

Adding a constant leaves deviations from the shifted mean unchanged.
Adding five to every value increases the standard deviation by five.
questions.explanation: Adding a constant leaves deviations from the shifted mean unchanged. The mean increases by five but SD does not. Spread and location respond differently to translations.

questions.prompt: Cosine rule for lengths and angles — Which statement gives the correct reasoning for this lesson?
options: The cross term is always added in the cosine rule.

questions.explanation: The rule is c²=a²+b²−2ab cosC. When C is obtuse its cosine is negative, so subtracting that negative term increases c². Retain the formula’s minus sign and evaluate the cosine separately.
